scope: renewed targeted public-evidence recovery and causal-triangulation audit for orientation, phyllary posture and stickiness; not a systematic review; not-recovered means not found in this search rather than proof of absence

public_Cirsium_context_added.source: Ohashi & Yahara 1998, American Journal of Botany
public_Cirsium_context_added.result: the study system has naturally nodding capitula and is pollinated predominantly by Bombus diversus; the paper quantifies pollinator responses to floral display rather than manipulating capitulum angle
public_Cirsium_context_added.use: shows that nodding Cirsium capitula remain compatible with effective legitimate visitation; it does not estimate an orientation effect

public_Cirsium_context_added.result: tagged Bombus diversus repeatedly visited naturally nodding Cirsium capitula across variation in floral display and neighbourhood density
public_Cirsium_context_added.use: within-genus pollination context only; no erect-versus-nodding comparison

closest_direct_manipulation.result: natural nodding versus artificially erect capitula; nodding heads had higher achene set, water and UV-B reduced pollen viability, no pollinator preference was detected between angle treatments, and no meaningful orientation-driven internal thermal difference was detected

orientation.current_best_public_inference: abiotic wetting/rain/UV-B reproductive protection remains the leading physical mechanism prior; static pollinator preference is not required to explain the closest manipulation and naturally nodding Cirsium heads can receive effective Bombus visitation
orientation.public_data_ceiling: direct focal-genus angle causation cannot be raised above an Asteraceae mechanism analog without a Cirsium head-angle manipulation linked to wetting/UV exposure, pollen viability and reproductive fitness
orientation.next_own_data_discriminator: randomized within-Cirsium head-angle manipulation with sham support; crossed or separately staged wetting/rain and UV exposure; pollen viability plus effective visitation/pollen transfer plus mature viable achene endpoints

structure_to_access_close_Cardueae.result: involucral-spine removal removed deterrence of illegitimate Lepidoptera and reduced filled seeds by 22%; legitimate bee/fly visitation frequency did not increase

enemy_interface_to_fitness_within_Cirsiu.result: Larinus planus oviposition is detectable as scars on phyllaries; infested capitula produced about 60% fewer mature seeds, about 40% fewer unfilled seeds, and lighter seeds
enemy_interface_to_fitness_within_Cirsiu.boundary: capitulum position and infestation were studied; phyllary geometry itself was not experimentally altered

legitimate_access_in_focal_appressed_sta.result: the natural appressed-phyllary state has documented bee, butterfly and hawkmoth visitors
legitimate_access_in_focal_appressed_sta.boundary: visitor occurrence is not effective pollen transfer and is not a posture manipulation

phyllary_posture.current_best_public_inference: mechanical antagonist-access control is strengthened by three-way triangulation: a close Cardueae structure manipulation changes illegitimate access and seed filling, a Cirsium seed predator uses the phyllary surface as an oviposition interface and strongly gates seed output, and focal appressed JPN36 remains accessible to legitimate visitors
phyllary_posture.public_data_ceiling: the missing causal edge is Cirsium phyllary/spine geometry -> antagonist or legitimate-visitor access; public evidence cannot supply that edge without a direct reversible focal-genus manipulation
phyllary_posture.next_own_data_discriminator: within-Cirsium reversible phyllary/access manipulation versus structure-matched sham, separating legitimate visitor access/effective transfer from seed-predator or florivore access/damage and carrying both to mature viable achene output

peer_reviewed_within_genus_evidence.result: occluding sticky bracteal exudates increased seed predation in Cirsium discolor in Illinois but had no detectable effect in Cirsium flodmani in Minnesota
later neutralization in Cirsium discolor did not increase seed predators, reduce predatory arthropods, or reduce successful seed production
pollinators did not contact sticky traps, several seed predators bypassed them, ants and aphids were deterred, and some predatory arthropods used sticky inflorescences

secondary_public_alternative_mechanism.source: Patricia A. Thomas dissertation, University of Illinois repository, The Function of Insect Trapping by Penstemon Digitalis and Cirsium Discolor
secondary_public_alternative_mechanism.result: radio-labelled prey experiments reported digestion, uptake and transport of nutrients from trapped insects and reproductive enhancement; for Cirsium discolor the trapped-insect N and P were estimated to represent only about 2-3% of seed N and P
secondary_public_alternative_mechanism.interpretation: nutrient subsidy is an additional mechanism worth measuring or excluding, but this secondary source does not overturn the peer-reviewed evidence for context-dependent and guild-selective effects

focal_JPN15_public_context.authority_source: National Museum of Nature and Science Japan Cirsium database
focal_JPN15_public_context.boundary: public occurrence and natural-history material do not identify which local guilds contact, avoid, bypass or benefit from the adhesive zone, nor the net seed-fitness effect

stickiness.current_best_public_inference: stickiness is already a direct within-Cirsium mechanism class, but its sign is context dependent and guild selective; the East-Asian causal question is now local context rather than generic function
stickiness.public_data_ceiling: no public dataset recovered that combines JPN15 stickiness manipulation, local arthropod guild response and reproductive fitness
stickiness.next_own_data_discriminator: within-JPN15 stickiness neutralization versus sham across replicated local contexts, with pretreatment guild characterization, treatment-induced changes in seed predators/herbivores/predators/ants/aphids/pollinators, mature viable seed output, treatment side-effect checks, and optional nutrient-status/captured-arthropod measurements to discriminate a nutrient-subsidy alternative

cross_trait_result.orientation: public evidence stops one edge before focal-genus causation
cross_trait_result.phyllary: public evidence now triangulates structure-access, Cirsium enemy-fitness and focal legitimate-access components but still lacks direct Cirsium structure manipulation
cross_trait_result.stickiness: within-genus mechanism is directly manipulated; only focal East-Asian context and net fitness sign remain unresolved
priority_for_new_biology: P02b within-JPN15 stickiness neutralization with local guild and fitness endpoints

public_data_stop_rule: Further broad public searching should not be treated as a substitute for the three focal manipulations. Re-open public recovery only for a newly located direct Cirsium head-angle manipulation, direct Cirsium phyllary/spine manipulation, or quantitative JPN15 manipulation/guild/fitness dataset.
claim_boundary: The triangulations rank mechanistic proximity and close specific causal edges. They do not transport effect sizes across taxa, establish historical selective causes, or prove adaptation in East-Asian Cirsium.
